chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

When that which came to al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) came to him, he entrusted his bequest to his daughter Fāṭimah outwardly, in a folded book. Then, when from the affair of al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) there occurred what occurred, she handed that over to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام).
I said to him, 'So what is in it, may Allah have mercy on you?' He said, 'What the children of Adam need from when the world came to be until it passes away.'

key_terms.ابْنَتِهِ: his daughter, through whom the trust was outwardly conveyed
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life from its beginning
key_terms.تَفْنَى: to perish or come to an end
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), the recipient of the bequest
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fāṭimah, the daughter entrusted with the bequest in appearance
key_terms.كِتَابٍ مُدْرَجٍ: a folded or sealed written document
key_terms.وُلْدُ آدَمَ: the children of Adam, meaning all human beings

ai.seo_question: How was Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (عليه السلام) bequest passed to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the outward transfer of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (عليه السلام) bequest to his daughter Fāṭimah, and then its delivery to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) after Karbala. It indicates the continuity of divinely guided authority and preserved knowledge with the Imams (عليهم السلام), and that the entrusted book contained all that humanity would need until the end of the world.
